global_context.prompt:
Task: Reconcile every raw skin-reaction assay or study description in this embedding neighborhood to a concise canonical assay/test context.

Rules:
- Consider all supplied values together and use the smallest scientifically defensible set of canonical labels.
- Multiple or all values may map to the same label. Values with the same core method must use exactly the same label.
- Keep genuinely different methods or study types separate, including human patch test, HRIPT, LLNA, GPMT, Buehler test, photopatch test, clinical observation, and case report.
- Merge spelling, formatting, and abbreviation variants of the same method.
- De-prioritize species, population, dose, vendor, readout, anatomical site, and incidental protocol wording unless it changes method identity.
- Do not infer a method not supported by the raw value. For vague values, use the shortest literal category supported by the text.
- Use concise lowercase scientific labels, normally one to four words.
- Never return unknown, unmapped, unspecified, null, or an explanation.
- Return every supplied ID exactly once and no additional IDs.

Examples:
human repeated-insult patch testing -> hript
Human Repeat Insult Patch Test (HRIPT) -> hript
local lymph node assay -> llna
guinea pig maximization test -> gpmt
clinical dermatology observation -> clinical observation
individual allergic contact dermatitis report -> case report

Output format:
{"mapping":{"<input_id>":"<canonical_context>"}}

global_species_context.prompt:
Task: Reconcile every raw skin-reaction species or population description in this embedding neighborhood to its canonical base experimental species.

Rules:
- Consider all supplied values together and use the smallest scientifically defensible set of canonical labels.
- Multiple or all values may map to the same label. Aliases for the same base species must use exactly the same label.
- Return only the base species; remove strain, sex, age, disease, treatment, anatomical site, and other population qualifiers.
- Treat clearly human clinical, demographic, occupational, or nationality descriptions as explicit support for human. Thus patients, children, nurses, hairdressers, and named human nationalities map to human rather than becoming separate labels.
- Normalize aliases and Latin names to concise lowercase common species names, such as canine to dog and porcine to pig.
- For multiple explicit species, deduplicate, alphabetize, and join them with ' + '.
- Do not infer a species from an assay name, cell line, reagent, or outside knowledge. Return 'no species' when no species or clearly human population is supported.
- Never return unknown, unmapped, unspecified, null, or an explanation.
- Return every supplied ID exactly once and no additional IDs.

Examples:
male Hartley guinea pigs -> guinea pig
Sprague-Dawley rat skin -> rat
human volunteers -> human
pediatric patients -> human
hairdressers with occupational dermatitis -> human
Caco-2 cells -> no species

Output format:
{"mapping":{"<input_id>":"<canonical_species_or_no_species>"}}

global_severity_grade.prompt:
Task: Classify every raw skin-reaction effect value in this embedding neighborhood using the fixed explicit-severity vocabulary below.

Rules:
- Consider all supplied values together and apply the same grade consistently to equivalent wording.
- Use only the JSON string labels '0', '1', '2', '3', '4', and 'no explicit grade'.
- Map 0 or explicit no reaction/negative to '0'; slight, minimal, weak, or mild to '1'; moderate to '2'; strong to '3'; and severe, very severe, extreme, or intense to '4'.
- Preserve an explicit numeric 0-4 or plus ladder (+ through ++++) at the corresponding grade.
- A generic positive result, positive patch test, percentage, count, range, or other value without an explicit ordinal grade is not a severity grade; return 'no explicit grade'.
- Do not infer severity from outcome direction, incidence, or outside context.
- Return every supplied ID exactly once and no additional IDs.

Output format:
{"mapping":{"<input_id>":"<0|1|2|3|4|no explicit grade>"}}

global_species_context.prompt:
Task: Assign the one canonical base species of the biological subject, tissue donor, or cell system that produced each reported skin-sensitization measurement. Each item contains assay_type, experimental_conditions, and support_text.

Rules:
- Consider all supplied values together and use the smallest scientifically defensible set of canonical labels.
- Multiple or all values may map to the same label.
- Read all three fields as one row-level evidence packet. Experimental conditions are normally the strongest evidence; use support text to confirm which organism produced the reported measurement.
- Return only one base species such as human, mouse, rat, guinea pig, rabbit, pig, dog, or cattle. Remove strain, sex, age, disease, treatment, anatomical site, and population qualifiers.
- A species is valid only when the packet ties it to the measured subject, donor tissue, primary cells, or experimental cell system. Explicitly human or animal cells may identify that system; do not infer a cell line's species from outside knowledge.
- Do not use organisms mentioned only as background, comparison, prior literature, reagents, serum, proteins, antibodies, substrates, or assay validation controls.
- Do not expand an acronym using outside knowledge. An assay name licenses a species only when the supplied words themselves state it.
- If different fields point to different possible experimental species, if several species are jointly studied, or if the measurement-producing species is unclear, return 'no species'. Never combine species.
- Normalize explicit aliases and Latin names to concise lowercase common species names.
- Return 'no species' when the packet does not explicitly and uniquely support the measurement-producing species.
- Never return unknown, unmapped, unspecified, null, an explanation, or text joined with '+'.
- Return every supplied ID exactly once and no additional IDs.

Examples:
assay_type=LLNA; experimental_conditions=female CBA mice; support_text=lymph-node proliferation was measured in treated mice -> mouse
assay_type=t-cell proliferation; experimental_conditions=human LLDC cultures; support_text=stimulation index was measured in LLDCs -> human
assay_type=peptide reactivity; experimental_conditions=synthetic peptide with bovine serum albumin reagent; support_text=no biological subject is identified -> no species
assay_type=skin diffusion; experimental_conditions=rat skin; support_text=the introduction compares rat and human skin but the reported flux used rat skin -> rat
assay_type=unspecified; experimental_conditions=mouse and rat tissues; support_text=pooled cross-species result -> no species

Output format:
{"mapping":{"<input_id>":"<one_canonical_species_or_no_species>"}}

global_endpoint_context.prompt:
Task: Reconcile every raw sensitization endpoint or target in this embedding neighborhood to the shortest specific canonical biological measurement concept.

Rules:
- Consider all supplied values together and use the smallest scientifically defensible set of canonical labels.
- Multiple or all values may map to the same label. Wording variants of the same biological measurement must use exactly the same label.
- Merge cysteine depletion with cysteine peptide depletion.
- Keep different nucleophiles separate: cysteine, lysine, and GSH/glutathione must not merge.
- Keep different biomarkers separate: CD86, CD54, and IL-8 must not merge.
- Keep EC3, stimulation index, keratinocyte activation, dendritic activation, and clinical sensitization distinct when stated.
- Remove species, assay, dose, instrument, vendor, and protocol qualifiers that do not change the measured concept.
- Do not infer an endpoint not supported by the raw value. Use concise lowercase scientific labels.
- Never return unknown, unmapped, unspecified, null, or an explanation.
- Return every supplied ID exactly once and no additional IDs.

Examples:
cysteine peptide depletion percent -> cysteine depletion
lysine peptide depletion -> lysine depletion
glutathione depletion -> gsh depletion
CD86 surface expression -> cd86
CD54 induction -> cd54
IL-8 release -> il-8

Output format:
{"mapping":{"<input_id>":"<canonical_endpoint>"}}

global_species_context.prompt:
Task: Reconcile every raw phototoxicity, irritation, or local-damage evidence_system in this embedding neighborhood to its canonical explicitly supported base biological subject or broad system.

Rules:
- Consider all supplied values together and use the smallest scientifically defensible set of canonical labels.
- Multiple or all values may map to the same label. Equivalent species or broad systems must use exactly the same label.
- Prefer a named base species when explicitly stated; clearly human clinical or population descriptions map to human.
- Otherwise use one of the supported broad concepts when stated: animal in vivo, in vitro cells, ex vivo tissue, reconstructed tissue, or non-biological/computational context.
- Remove strain, sex, age, anatomical site, tissue layer, and protocol qualifiers.
- Do not infer an unstated species from a cell line, assay, reagent, or outside knowledge.
- Return 'no species or system' only when the value supports neither a species nor a broad system.
- Never return unknown, unmapped, unspecified, null, or an explanation.
- Return every supplied ID exactly once and no additional IDs.

Output format:
{"mapping":{"<input_id>":"<canonical_species_or_system>"}}
